Although I can build jar file now, I still have some warning errors like: error: package org.openarchives.oai._2 does not exist. Actually those packages are in target/generated-sources, and this path is in my build path. I don't know why javadoc can not find it. I tried several ways, but all failed.
At the mean time, I will try to submit a pull-request today, so that we can test if the jar can be built on other's machine.

The version I created pull-request won't work either. I checked on Java 8. And the reason is Javadoc in Java 8 is stricter on the requirements. I tried to disable the strict checking, and it works on Java 8. I am trying to fix the error today to see if I can let Java 8 happy.

Closed PR-13 due to the extreme number of unrelated updates to this ticket.
Please create a new PR that only contains javadoc-related updates.

See attached "javadoc.out" for the errors I am seeing when running:
`mvn javadoc:jar`

That's the part I need help, since it is a dynamic import. Those classes or interfaces actually in target directory. That's why there is no warning showing in the second time. Please let me know if you know how to fix it.

Thanks!
I added the excludePackageNames in pom.xml. Please check.

You are on the right track. Here is a PR off of your work with some minor modifications:
https://github.com/nianma/fcrepo4-oaiprovider/pull/1

I still get warnings if I run:
`mvn clean javadoc:jar`

...but the javadocs are successfully created.
However, if I run:
`mvn clean javadoc:javadoc; mvn javadoc:jar`
...there are no warnings.

In any case, I think it should work in the important case of running the release tasks.

Getting weird. I had no warning by running 'mvn clean javadoc:jar'. Not so sure what's different in my setting. Following is the output:
